fr: Beaucoup d'étudiants ont réussi leur examen cette année.
en: Many students passed their exam this year.
ipa: /bo.ku de.ty.djɑ̃ ɔ̃ ʁe.y.si lœʁ ɛg.za.mɛ̃ sɛt a.ne/
notes: De becomes d' before a vowel sound in d'étudiants, a spelling learners often forget.

fr: Il faut que tu manges un peu de légumes à chaque repas.
en: You must eat a little vegetables at each meal.
ipa: /il fo kə ty mɑ̃ʒ œ̃ pø də le.gym a ʃak ʁə.pa/
notes: The final s in manges is silent, easy to drop when writing from dictation.

fr: Plusieurs collègues se sont plaints du bruit dans le bureau.
en: Several colleagues complained about the noise in the office.
ipa: /ply.zjœʁ kɔ.lɛg sə sɔ̃ plɛ̃ dy bʁɥi dɑ̃ lə by.ʁo/
notes: Se sont plaints uses the reflexive se, easily confused with the demonstrative ce when writing quickly.

fr: La plupart des touristes visitent ce quartier au printemps.
en: Most tourists visit this neighborhood in spring.
ipa: /la ply.paʁ de tu.ʁist vi.zit sə kaʁ.tje o pʁɛ̃.tɑ̃/
notes: The liaison between des and touristes adds a z sound that beginners sometimes forget to link.

fr: Tous les élèves doivent rendre leur devoir avant vendredi.
en: All the students must hand in their homework before Friday.
ipa: /tu le ze.lɛv dwav ʁɑ̃dʁ lœʁ də.vwaʁ a.vɑ̃ vɑ̃.dʁə.di/
notes: In tous les élèves, the s of tous stays silent while the s of les links to the vowel, a common liaison mix-up.

fr: Quelques amis sont venus me rendre visite hier soir.
en: A few friends came to visit me last night.
ipa: /kɛl.kə.z‿a.mi sɔ̃ və.ny mə ʁɑ̃dʁ vi.zit jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: The s at the end of quelques is silent alone but links as a z sound before the vowel in amis.

fr: Nous avons assez de temps pour finir ce projet ensemble.
en: We have enough time to finish this project together.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ a.se də tɑ̃ puʁ fi.niʁ sə pʁɔ.ʒɛ ɑ̃.sɑ̃blə/
notes: The nasal vowels in temps and ensemble sound similar and are often misspelled by learners.

fr: Il y a trop de bruit dans cette rue le samedi soir.
en: There is too much noise in this street on Saturday evenings.
ipa: /il i a tʁo də bʁɥi dɑ̃ sɛt ʁy lə sam.di swaʁ/
notes: The final p in trop is always silent, a spelling trap when writing from sound.

fr: Peu de gens connaissent la véritable histoire de ce village.
en: Few people know the true story of this village.
ipa: /pø də ʒɑ̃ kɔ.nɛs la ve.ʁi.tabl is.twaʁ də sə vi.laʒ/
notes: The ent ending of connaissent is completely silent, a frequent dictation error.

fr: Une dizaine de personnes attendaient devant la porte du magasin.
en: About ten people were waiting in front of the shop door.
ipa: /yn di.zɛn də pɛʁ.sɔn a.tɑ̃.dɛ də.vɑ̃ la pɔʁt dy ma.ga.zɛ̃/
notes: The imperfect ending aient in attendaient is pronounced like an open e but spelled with four silent letters.

fr: La moitié de la classe a choisi l'option espagnol.
en: Half the class chose the Spanish option.
ipa: /la mwa.tje də la klas a ʃwa.zi lɔp.sjɔ̃ ɛs.pa.ɲɔl/
notes: L'option drops the e of la before a vowel, a spelling learners often miss.

fr: Aucune excuse ne justifie ce genre de comportement.
en: No excuse justifies that kind of behavior.
ipa: /o.kyn ɛk.skyz nə ʒys.ti.fi sə ʒɑ̃ʁ də kɔ̃.pɔʁ.tə.mɑ̃/
notes: Ce here is the demonstrative adjective before genre, not the reflexive se, a pairing that trips up spelling.

fr: Chaque élève doit apporter ses propres crayons de couleur.
en: Each student must bring their own colored pencils.
ipa: /ʃak e.lɛv dwa a.pɔʁ.te se pʁɔpʁ kʁɛ.jɔ̃ də ku.lœʁ/
notes: Ses (possessive) sounds exactly like ces and c'est, so context alone decides the spelling.

fr: La majorité des habitants soutient ce nouveau projet municipal.
en: The majority of residents support this new municipal project.
ipa: /la ma.ʒɔ.ʁi.te de.z‿a.bi.tɑ̃ su.tjɛ̃ sə nu.vo pʁɔ.ʒɛ my.ni.si.pal/
notes: Des links to habitants with a z sound, easy to omit in dictation.

fr: L'ensemble des employés a reçu une prime exceptionnelle.
en: All the employees received an exceptional bonus.
ipa: /lɑ̃.sɑ̃blə de.z‿ɑ̃.plwa.je a ʁə.sy yn pʁim ɛk.sɛp.sjɔ.nɛl/
notes: L'ensemble contracts le before the vowel-starting ensemble, a common elision to remember.

fr: Beaucoup de touristes pensent que ce musée ferme le lundi.
en: Many tourists think that this museum closes on Mondays.
ipa: /bo.ku də tu.ʁist pɑ̃s kə sə my.ze fɛʁm lə lœ̃.di/
notes: The nasal en in pensent is easy to misspell as an or in when writing quickly.

fr: Il faut que nous fassions un peu plus d'efforts collectifs.
en: We must make a little more collective effort.
ipa: /il fo kə nu fa.sjɔ̃ œ̃ pø plys d‿e.fɔʁ kɔ.lɛk.tif/
notes: Fassions is the irregular subjunctive of faire, easy to misspell as the indicative faisons.

fr: Bien que plusieurs solutions existent, aucune ne convainc vraiment.
en: Although several solutions exist, none really convinces us.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə ply.zjœʁ sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ ɛg.zist o.kyn nə kɔ̃.vɛ̃k vʁɛ.mɑ̃/
notes: Existent must agree with the plural solutions even though the subjunctive after bien que sounds identical to the indicative here.

fr: Trop de gens gaspillent de la nourriture chaque jour.
en: Too many people waste food every day.
ipa: /tʁo də ʒɑ̃ gas.pij də la nu.ʁi.tyʁ ʃak ʒuʁ/
notes: The final ent of gaspillent is silent, a frequent dictée trap for third person plural verbs.

fr: Assez d'élèves ont échoué pour inquiéter les professeurs.
en: Enough students failed to worry the teachers.
ipa: /a.se de.lɛv ɔ̃ e.ʃwe puʁ ɛ̃.kje.te le pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ/
notes: De becomes d' before the vowel in élèves, a spelling detail lost when only listening.

fr: Chaque fois que nous sortons, il pleut des cordes.
en: Every time we go out, it rains cats and dogs.
ipa: /ʃak fwa kə nu sɔʁ.tɔ̃ il plø de kɔʁd/
notes: The nasal on in sortons is easy to confuse with the an sound when transcribing quickly.

fr: La plupart du temps, elle préférait rester à la maison.
en: Most of the time, she preferred to stay home.
ipa: /la ply.paʁ dy tɑ̃ ɛl pʁe.fe.ʁɛ ʁɛs.te a la mɛ.zɔ̃/
notes: Préférait needs two acute accents on the e's, easy to drop when writing fast from dictation.

fr: Il reste peu de places disponibles pour ce concert.
en: There are few seats left available for this concert.
ipa: /il ʁɛst pø də plas dis.pɔ.nibl puʁ sə kɔ̃.sɛʁ/
notes: Ce before concert is the demonstrative adjective, not the reflexive pronoun se, though both sound identical.

fr: Toutes les fenêtres doivent rester fermées pendant la nuit.
en: All the windows must stay closed during the night.
ipa: /tut le fə.nɛtʁ dwav ʁɛs.te fɛʁ.me pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la nɥi/
notes: Fenêtres carries a circumflex accent on the e, a silent mark that only shows in writing.

fr: Beaucoup de familles quittent la ville pendant les vacances d'été.
en: Many families leave the city during the summer holidays.
ipa: /bo.ku də fa.mij kit la vil pɑ̃.dɑ̃ le va.kɑ̃s de.te/
notes: De contracts to d'été before the vowel, a small elision that is easy to miss in dictation.

fr: Il doute que plusieurs candidats soient prêts pour l'entretien.
en: He doubts that several candidates are ready for the interview.
ipa: /il dut kə ply.zjœʁ kɑ̃.di.da swa pʁɛ puʁ lɑ̃.tʁə.tjɛ̃/
notes: Soient is the subjunctive plural of être, spelled with a silent ent that sounds just like soit.

fr: Un peu de patience suffit pour apprendre cette langue.
en: A little patience is enough to learn this language.
ipa: /œ̃ pø də pa.sjɑ̃s sy.fi puʁ a.pʁɑ̃dʁ sɛt lɑ̃g/
notes: The ti in patience is pronounced like an s sound, a spelling pattern that easily misleads.

fr: Chaque élève de cette classe mérite une attention particulière.
en: Every student in this class deserves special attention.
ipa: /ʃak e.lɛv də sɛt klas me.ʁit yn a.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ paʁ.ti.ky.ljɛʁ/
notes: Particulière ends in a grave accent on the e before re, often forgotten in fast dictation.

fr: La plupart des enfants aiment jouer dehors quand il fait beau.
en: Most children like to play outside when the weather is nice.
ipa: /la ply.paʁ de.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ɛm ʒwe də.ɔʁ kɑ̃ il fɛ bo/
notes: Des links to enfants with a z sound, a liaison that is invisible unless you know the rule.

fr: Il n'y a aucune raison de s'inquiéter pour ce retard.
en: There is no reason to worry about this delay.
ipa: /il nj a o.kyn ʁɛ.zɔ̃ də sɛ̃.kje.te puʁ sə ʁə.taʁ/
notes: Se contracts to s' before inquiéter because the verb starts with a vowel.

fr: Quelques minutes suffisent pour réchauffer ce plat au four.
en: A few minutes are enough to reheat this dish in the oven.
ipa: /kɛl.kə mi.nyt sy.fiz puʁ ʁe.ʃo.fe sə pla o fuʁ/
notes: Suffisent ends in a silent ent, the same trap as most third person plural present verbs.

fr: Nous avons trop de valises pour ce petit coffre.
en: We have too many suitcases for this small trunk.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ tʁo də va.liz puʁ sə pə.ti kɔfʁ/
notes: Coffre keeps a double f, a spelling detail that pronunciation alone does not reveal.

fr: Assez de personnes ont signé la pétition pour sauver le parc.
en: Enough people signed the petition to save the park.
ipa: /a.se də pɛʁ.sɔn ɔ̃ si.ɲe la pe.ti.sjɔ̃ puʁ so.ve lə paʁk/
notes: Pétition carries an acute accent on the first e, easily dropped when writing from sound.

fr: Il se peut que peu de gens acceptent cette proposition.
en: It may be that few people accept this proposal.
ipa: /il sə pø kə pø də ʒɑ̃ ak.sɛpt sɛt pʁɔ.po.zi.sjɔ̃/
notes: Acceptent is the subjunctive plural after il se peut que, its silent ent ending easy to forget.

fr: Une dizaine d'oiseaux se sont posés sur le toit.
en: About ten birds landed on the roof.
ipa: /yn di.zɛn dwa.zo sə sɔ̃ po.ze syʁ lə twa/
notes: De contracts to d'oiseaux before the vowel sound, a common elision in counted quantities.

fr: La moitié des invités n'est pas encore arrivée.
en: Half the guests have not yet arrived.
ipa: /la mwa.tje de.z‿ɛ̃.vi.te nɛ pa.z‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ a.ʁi.ve/
notes: Des links to invités with a z sound that many learners forget to pronounce or transcribe.

fr: Aucun élève n'a compris cette règle de grammaire.
en: No student understood this grammar rule.
ipa: /o.kœ̃.n‿e.lɛv na kɔ̃.pʁi sɛt ʁɛgl də gʁa.mɛʁ/
notes: Aucun links with a hidden n sound before élève, a liaison that changes how the phrase sounds.

fr: Chaque semaine, la plupart des employés télétravaillent deux jours.
en: Each week, most employees work from home two days.
ipa: /ʃak sə.mɛn la ply.paʁ de.z‿ɑ̃.plwa.je te.le.tʁa.vaj dø ʒuʁ/
notes: Employés begins with the nasal em sound, often confused with an in quick dictation.

fr: La majorité de ses collègues ignoraient la nouvelle règle.
en: The majority of his colleagues did not know the new rule.
ipa: /la ma.ʒɔ.ʁi.te də se kɔ.lɛg i.ɲɔ.ʁɛ la nu.vɛl ʁɛgl/
notes: Ses here is the possessive adjective, not ces or c'est, though all three sound the same.

fr: L'ensemble du personnel a suivi la formation obligatoire.
en: The entire staff attended the mandatory training.
ipa: /lɑ̃.sɑ̃blə dy pɛʁ.sɔ.nɛl a sɥi.vi la fɔʁ.ma.sjɔ̃ ɔ.bli.ga.twaʁ/
notes: L'ensemble is always contracted because ensemble starts with a vowel sound.

fr: Beaucoup de gens croient que ce climat va empirer.
en: Many people believe that this climate will worsen.
ipa: /bo.ku də ʒɑ̃ kʁwa kə sə kli.ma va ɑ̃.pi.ʁe/
notes: Croient ends in a silent ent even though it is pronounced the same as the singular croit.

fr: Il faut que chaque participant apporte quelques idées nouvelles.
en: Each participant must bring a few new ideas.
ipa: /il fo kə ʃak paʁ.ti.si.pɑ̃ a.pɔʁt kɛl.kə.z‿i.de nu.vɛl/
notes: Apporte is the subjunctive of apporter, spelled without an s even though the subject sounds singular.

fr: Trop de bruit empêche les élèves de se concentrer.
en: Too much noise prevents the students from concentrating.
ipa: /tʁo də bʁɥi ɑ̃.pɛʃ le.z‿e.lɛv də sə kɔ̃.sɑ̃.tʁe/
notes: Empêche carries a circumflex on the e, a silent accent mark impossible to hear.

fr: Assez de neige est tombée pour fermer les routes.
en: Enough snow fell to close the roads.
ipa: /a.se də nɛʒ ɛ tɔ̃.be puʁ fɛʁ.me le ʁut/
notes: Tombée agrees in the feminine with neige because the verb tomber uses être in the passé composé.

fr: Peu de solutions existent pour résoudre ce problème rapidement.
en: Few solutions exist to solve this problem quickly.
ipa: /pø də sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ ɛg.zist puʁ ʁe.zudʁ sə pʁɔ.blɛm ʁa.pid.mɑ̃/
notes: Existent ends with a silent ent, the classic third person plural trap.

fr: La plupart des voisins se plaignent du chantier voisin.
en: Most neighbors complain about the nearby construction site.
ipa: /la ply.paʁ de vwa.zɛ̃ sə plɛɲ dy ʃɑ̃.tje vwa.zɛ̃/
notes: Se plaignent uses the reflexive se, not the demonstrative ce, despite the identical sound.

fr: Tous les documents doivent être signés avant vendredi.
en: All the documents must be signed before Friday.
ipa: /tu le dɔ.ky.mɑ̃ dwav.t‿ɛtʁ si.ɲe a.vɑ̃ vɑ̃.dʁə.di/
notes: The s of les links to documents while the s of tous remains silent, a frequent liaison confusion.

fr: Une dizaine de messages attendaient une réponse ce matin.
en: About ten messages were waiting for a reply this morning.
ipa: /yn di.zɛn də mɛ.saʒ a.tɑ̃.dɛ yn ʁe.pɔ̃s sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: The imperfect ending aient in attendaient is nasal but spelled with several silent letters.

fr: Il est possible que la moitié des candidats abandonnent.
en: It is possible that half the candidates will give up.
ipa: /il ɛ pɔ.sibl kə la mwa.tje de kɑ̃.di.da a.bɑ̃.dɔn/
notes: Abandonnent is subjunctive here, its silent ent ending easy to mishear as singular.

fr: Chaque client reçoit une facture détaillée à la fin du mois.
en: Each customer receives a detailed invoice at the end of the month.
ipa: /ʃak kli.jɑ̃ ʁə.swa yn fak.tyʁ de.ta.je a la fɛ̃ dy mwa/
notes: Reçoit needs a cedilla under the c to keep the soft s sound before o.

fr: Beaucoup d'habitants craignent que ce projet ne détruise le quartier.
en: Many residents fear that this project will destroy the neighborhood.
ipa: /bo.ku da.bi.tɑ̃ kʁɛɲ kə sə pʁɔ.ʒɛ nə de.tʁɥiz lə kaʁ.tje/
notes: De elides to d' before habitants, even though the h is silent and sounds like a vowel.

fr: Il ne reste que peu de temps avant la fin des inscriptions.
en: There is only a little time left before registration closes.
ipa: /il nə ʁɛst kə pø də tɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ la fɛ̃ de.z‿ɛ̃s.kʁip.sjɔ̃/
notes: Des links to inscriptions with a z sound, easy to skip when writing quickly.

fr: La plupart des recettes demandent un peu de sel et de poivre.
en: Most recipes call for a little salt and pepper.
ipa: /la ply.paʁ de ʁə.sɛt də.mɑ̃d œ̃ pø də sɛl e də pwavʁ/
notes: Recettes doubles the t, a spelling detail that the pronunciation does not indicate.

fr: Aucune de ces excuses ne me convainc vraiment.
en: None of these excuses really convinces me.
ipa: /o.kyn də se.z‿ɛk.skyz nə mə kɔ̃.vɛ̃k vʁɛ.mɑ̃/
notes: Ces here is the plural demonstrative, distinct in spelling from ses and c'est despite sounding alike.

fr: Chaque année, plusieurs espèces disparaissent à cause du réchauffement.
en: Each year, several species disappear because of global warming.
ipa: /ʃak a.ne ply.zjœʁ ɛs.pɛs dis.pa.ʁɛs a koz dy ʁe.ʃof.mɑ̃/
notes: Disparaissent ends in a silent ent, the standard third person plural ending.

fr: L'ensemble des données a été analysé par les chercheurs.
en: The entire set of data was analyzed by the researchers.
ipa: /lɑ̃.sɑ̃blə de dɔ.ne a e.te a.na.li.ze paʁ le ʃɛʁ.ʃœʁ/
notes: Analysé stays masculine singular because it agrees with ensemble, not with the plural données.

fr: Trop de touristes visitent ce site fragile chaque été.
en: Too many tourists visit this fragile site every summer.
ipa: /tʁo də tu.ʁist vi.zit sə sit fʁaʒil ʃak e.te/
notes: Visitent takes the silent ent plural ending, easy to miss when the subject sounds singular in speech.

fr: Un peu de sucre suffit pour adoucir cette sauce.
en: A little sugar is enough to sweeten this sauce.
ipa: /œ̃ pø də sykʁ sy.fi puʁ a.du.siʁ sɛt sos/
notes: Adoucir has no double letters despite sounding heavy, a common overspelling mistake.

fr: Il semble que quelques erreurs se soient glissées dans le rapport.
en: It seems that a few errors slipped into the report.
ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə kɛl.kə.z‿ɛ.ʁœʁ sə swa gli.se dɑ̃ lə ʁa.pɔʁ/
notes: Glissées agrees in the feminine plural with erreurs in this reflexive past subjunctive construction.

fr: La majorité des clients préfèrent payer par carte.
en: The majority of customers prefer to pay by card.
ipa: /la ma.ʒɔ.ʁi.te de kli.jɑ̃ pʁe.fɛʁ pe.je paʁ kaʁt/
notes: Préfèrent needs a grave accent on the first e, which many learners drop when writing fast.

fr: Chaque matin, il boit un peu de café avant de partir.
en: Every morning, he drinks a little coffee before leaving.
ipa: /ʃak ma.tɛ̃ il bwa œ̃ pø də ka.fe a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ/
notes: Matin ends in a nasal in sound, easily confused with the ain or ein spelling patterns.

fr: Beaucoup de voyageurs attendent que l'avion décolle enfin.
en: Many travelers are waiting for the plane to finally take off.
ipa: /bo.ku də vwa.ja.ʒœʁ a.tɑ̃d kə la.vjɔ̃ de.kɔl ɑ̃.fɛ̃/
notes: Décolle is subjunctive after attendre que, spelled with a double l even though it sounds short.

fr: Il n'y a que peu de chances que ce plan fonctionne.
en: There is only a small chance that this plan will work.
ipa: /il nj a kə pø də ʃɑ̃s kə sə plɑ̃ fɔ̃k.sjɔn/
notes: Ce plan uses the demonstrative ce, not the reflexive se, though they are pronounced identically.

fr: Toutes les preuves indiquent que plusieurs suspects mentent.
en: All the evidence indicates that several suspects are lying.
ipa: /tut le pʁœv ɛ̃.dik kə ply.zjœʁ sys.pɛ mɑ̃t/
notes: Mentent doubles the final consonant before the silent ent ending, unlike the singular ment.

fr: Assez de preuves ont été rassemblées pour rouvrir l'enquête.
en: Enough evidence has been gathered to reopen the investigation.
ipa: /a.se də pʁœv ɔ̃.t‿e.te ʁa.sɑ̃.ble puʁ ʁu.vʁiʁ lɑ̃.kɛt/
notes: La contracts to l' before enquête because the word begins with a vowel sound.

fr: La plupart du personnel ignore encore les nouvelles règles.
en: Most of the staff still does not know the new rules.
ipa: /la ply.paʁ dy pɛʁ.sɔ.nɛl i.ɲɔʁ ɑ̃.kɔʁ le nu.vɛl ʁɛgl/
notes: Encore opens with a nasal en sound that is often written as an by mistake.

fr: Il faut que la moitié des équipes changent de stratégie.
en: Half the teams must change their strategy.
ipa: /il fo kə la mwa.tje de.z‿e.kip ʃɑ̃ʒ də stʁa.te.ʒi/
notes: Changent is subjunctive plural, its silent ent easy to drop after the singular sounding équipe.

fr: Aucun résultat ne confirme cette hypothèse pour l'instant.
en: No result confirms this hypothesis for now.
ipa: /o.kœ̃ ʁe.zyl.ta nə kɔ̃.fiʁm sɛt i.pɔ.tɛz puʁ lɛ̃s.tɑ̃/
notes: Le contracts to l' before instant, since the word starts with a vowel sound.

fr: Chaque soir, quelques voisins se retrouvent sur la terrasse.
en: Every evening, a few neighbors meet on the terrace.
ipa: /ʃak swaʁ kɛl.kə vwa.zɛ̃ sə ʁə.tʁuv syʁ la tɛ.ʁas/
notes: Se retrouvent is reflexive and spelled with se, not the demonstrative ce.

fr: La majorité des enseignants souhaitent plus de moyens.
en: The majority of teachers want more resources.
ipa: /la ma.ʒɔ.ʁi.te de.z‿ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃ swɛt plys də mwa.jɛ̃/
notes: Des links to enseignants with a z sound that only appears because the noun starts with a vowel.

fr: L'ensemble de la classe attend avec impatience les résultats.
en: The whole class is waiting impatiently for the results.
ipa: /lɑ̃.sɑ̃blə də la klas a.tɑ̃ a.vɛk ɛ̃.pa.sjɑ̃s le ʁe.zyl.ta/
notes: Impatience opens with a nasal im sound, a spelling that beginners often confuse with en.

fr: Trop de publicités interrompent la vidéo toutes les deux minutes.
en: Too many ads interrupt the video every two minutes.
ipa: /tʁo də py.bli.si.te ɛ̃.te.ʁɔ̃p la vi.de.o tut le dø mi.nyt/
notes: Toutes les links the s of toutes and les together before deux, forming a chain of liaisons.

fr: Un peu de courage suffit pour affronter cette situation.
en: A little courage is enough to face this situation.
ipa: /œ̃ pø də ku.ʁaʒ sy.fi puʁ a.fʁɔ̃.te sɛt si.tɥa.sjɔ̃/
notes: Affronter doubles the f, a spelling detail invisible when only hearing the word.

fr: Il doute que peu de collègues acceptent ce changement d'horaire sans protester.
en: He doubts that few colleagues will accept this schedule change without protesting.
ipa: /il dut kə pø də kɔ.lɛg ak.sɛpt sə ʃɑ̃ʒ.mɑ̃ dɔ.ʁɛʁ sɑ̃ pʁɔ.tɛs.te/
notes: Acceptent takes the silent ent subjunctive ending after il doute que.

fr: Quelle drôle d'idée d'inviter autant de monde ce soir.
en: What a strange idea to invite so many people tonight.
ipa: /kɛl dʁol di.de dɛ̃.vi.te o.tɑ̃ də mɔ̃d sə swaʁ/
notes: Quelle takes the feminine e because idée is feminine, unlike the masculine quel.

fr: Chaque proposition mérite d'être étudiée avec attention.
en: Every proposal deserves to be studied carefully.
ipa: /ʃak pʁɔ.po.zi.sjɔ̃ me.ʁit dɛtʁ e.ty.dje a.vɛk a.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃/
notes: De contracts to d' before être since the verb begins with a vowel sound.

fr: La plupart des animaux du zoo dorment pendant la journée.
en: Most of the zoo animals sleep during the day.
ipa: /la ply.paʁ de.z‿a.ni.mo dy zo dɔʁm pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la ʒuʁ.ne/
notes: Des links to animaux with a z sound that changes how the phrase is pronounced.

fr: Il faudrait que toutes les fenêtres soient nettoyées avant la visite.
en: All the windows should be cleaned before the visit.
ipa: /il fo.dʁɛ kə tut le fə.nɛtʁ swa nɛ.twa.je a.vɑ̃ la vi.zit/
notes: Nettoyées agrees in the feminine plural with fenêtres in this passive subjunctive construction.

fr: Bien que la plupart des experts s'accordent, quelques divergences subsistent encore.
en: Although most experts agree, a few disagreements still remain.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə la ply.paʁ de.z‿ɛks.pɛʁ sa.kɔʁd kɛl.kə di.vɛʁ.ʒɑ̃s syb.zist ɑ̃.kɔʁ/
notes: Se contracts to s' before accordent because the verb starts with a vowel sound.

fr: Il se peut que la majorité des salariés ignorent leurs droits exacts.
en: It may be that most employees do not know their exact rights.
ipa: /il sə pø kə la ma.ʒɔ.ʁi.te de sa.la.ʁje i.ɲɔʁ lœʁ dʁwa ɛg.za/
notes: Ignorent is subjunctive plural after il se peut que, its silent ent ending often forgotten.

fr: Quoi qu'il en soit, aucune de ces hypothèses ne tient réellement debout.
en: Whatever the case, none of these hypotheses really holds up.
ipa: /kwa kil ɑ̃ swa o.kyn də se.z‿i.pɔ.tɛz nə tjɛ̃ ʁe.ɛl.mɑ̃ də.bu/
notes: Ces here is the plural demonstrative, not ses or c'est, even though all three sound alike.

fr: Pour que l'ensemble du dossier soit accepté, il manque encore une signature.
en: For the whole file to be accepted, one signature is still missing.
ipa: /puʁ kə lɑ̃.sɑ̃blə dy dɔ.sje swa.t‿ak.sɛp.te il mɑ̃k ɑ̃.kɔʁ yn si.ɲa.tyʁ/
notes: Le contracts to l' before ensemble since the noun begins with a vowel sound.

fr: Il est peu probable que chaque associé accepte cette clause sans négocier.
en: It is unlikely that each partner will accept this clause without negotiating.
ipa: /il ɛ pø pʁɔ.babl kə ʃak a.sɔ.sje ak.sɛpt sɛt kloz sɑ̃ ne.gɔ.sje/
notes: Accepte stays in the singular subjunctive because chaque associé is grammatically singular despite implying many people.

fr: Bien que peu de candidats aient réussi, le jury reste satisfait du niveau.
en: Although few candidates succeeded, the jury remains satisfied with the level.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə pø də kɑ̃.di.da e ʁe.y.si lə ʒy.ʁi ʁɛst sa.tis.fɛ dy ni.vo/
notes: Aient is the subjunctive of avoir, spelled with a silent ent that sounds identical to a singular ait.

fr: La moitié des salariés craint que ce plan social ne supprime des postes.
en: Half the employees fear that this restructuring plan will eliminate positions.
ipa: /la mwa.tje de sa.la.ʁje kʁɛ̃ kə sə plɑ̃ sɔ.sjal nə sy.pʁim de pɔst/
notes: Ce plan uses the demonstrative adjective ce, not the reflexive pronoun se, despite the identical pronunciation.

fr: Quelle que soit la raison, trop de décisions sont prises dans la précipitation.
en: Whatever the reason, too many decisions are made in haste.
ipa: /kɛl kə swa la ʁɛ.zɔ̃ tʁo də de.si.zjɔ̃ sɔ̃ pʁiz dɑ̃ la pʁe.si.pi.ta.sjɔ̃/
notes: Quelle que soit agrees in the feminine with raison, unlike the invariable quel que in other contexts.

fr: Il n'existe aucun consensus, bien que la plupart des chercheurs partagent la même hypothèse.
en: There is no consensus, although most researchers share the same hypothesis.
ipa: /il nɛg.zist o.kœ̃ kɔ̃.sɑ̃.sys bjɛ̃ kə la ply.paʁ de ʃɛʁ.ʃœʁ paʁ.taʒ la mɛm i.pɔ.tɛz/
notes: Hypothèse begins with a silent h and carries a grave accent, both invisible to the ear.

fr: Bien que l'entreprise ait embauché une dizaine de stagiaires, peu d'entre eux resteront.
en: Although the company hired about ten interns, few of them will stay.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə lɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz ɛ ɑ̃.bo.ʃe yn di.zɛn də sta.ʒjɛʁ pø dɑ̃tʁ ø ʁɛs.tə.ʁɔ̃/
notes: De contracts to d'entre before the vowel sound, a subtler elision than the more common d'un or d'une.

fr: Il se pourrait que l'ensemble des mesures annoncées soit insuffisant.
en: It could be that all the announced measures are insufficient.
ipa: /il sə puʁ.ʁɛ kə lɑ̃.sɑ̃blə de mə.zyʁ a.nɔ̃.se swa.t‿ɛ̃.sy.fi.zɑ̃/
notes: Soit stays singular because the subject is ensemble, even though mesures is plural.

fr: Quoiqu'il y ait assez de preuves, aucune poursuite n'a encore été engagée.
en: Although there is enough evidence, no legal action has been taken yet.
ipa: /kwa.kil i ɛ a.se də pʁœv o.kyn puʁ.sɥit na ɑ̃.kɔʁ e.te ɑ̃.ga.ʒe/
notes: Quoique contracts to quoiqu' before il because the pronoun begins with a vowel sound.

fr: Peu s'en faut que la totalité du budget ne soit dépassée cette année.
en: It would not take much for the entire budget to be exceeded this year.
ipa: /pø sɑ̃ fo kə la tɔ.ta.li.te dy by.dʒɛ nə swa de.pa.se sɛt a.ne/
notes: Dépassée doubles the s to keep the unvoiced sound, and agrees in the feminine with totalité.

fr: Bien que chaque service ait ses propres priorités, tous doivent respecter le même délai.
en: Although each department has its own priorities, all must respect the same deadline.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə ʃak sɛʁ.vis ɛ se pʁɔpʁ pʁi.jɔ.ʁi.te tus dwav ʁɛs.pɛk.te lə mɛm de.lɛ/
notes: Ses is the possessive here, spelled differently from the homophones ces and c'est.

fr: Il semblerait que la majorité des actionnaires s'oppose à cette fusion.
en: It would seem that the majority of shareholders oppose this merger.
ipa: /il sɑ̃.blə.ʁɛ kə la ma.ʒɔ.ʁi.te de.z‿ak.sjɔ.nɛʁ sɔ.poz a sɛt fy.zjɔ̃/
notes: Se contracts to s' before oppose because the verb begins with a vowel sound.

fr: Aussi peu convaincant que cela paraisse, plusieurs experts soutiennent cette thèse.
en: As unconvincing as it may seem, several experts support this thesis.
ipa: /o.si pø kɔ̃.vɛ̃.kɑ̃ kə sə.la pa.ʁɛs ply.zjœʁ ɛks.pɛʁ su.tjɛn sɛt tɛz/
notes: Thèse begins with a silent h after the t, a spelling that gives no clue in pronunciation.

fr: Que la moitié du conseil s'abstienne ne changera rien à la décision finale.
en: Whether half the council abstains will change nothing about the final decision.
ipa: /kə la mwa.tje dy kɔ̃.sɛj sap.stjɛn nə ʃɑ̃ʒ.ʁa ʁjɛ̃ a la de.si.zjɔ̃ fi.nal/
notes: Se contracts to s' before abstienne, a reflexive elision easy to miss in a subjunctive clause.
